title.narrative: Multi-sectoral lifesaving intervention to reduce malnutrition in Yirgachefe Woreda of Gedio Zone, South Ethiopia Region (Priority 1)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed 9-month project will strengthen access to lifesaving and life-sustaining multisectoral services to reduce malnutrition in Yirgachefe, in line with HRP 2024 and allocation Priority 1. Through targeted nutrition, health, WASH, and agricultural interventions, the project will focus on service provision for most vulnerable groups who have limited access to regular services. The project addresses needs and critical gaps of 179 908 (= Men= 44,724 Women=85,261 Boys=24,291 Girls= 25,632) vulnerable communities in Yirgachefe Woreda . According to the GOAL Ethiopia rapid-specific assessment conducted in July 2024 in Yirgachefe Woreda, the needs assessment highlights an increase in SAM (severe acute malnutrition) admissions in June 2024 as compared with the same months of last year, which increased by 175 (65%). Malaria, Cholera, Scabies, Trachoma, and Measles are reported as important public health diseases in the woreda, which are repeatedly reported, including an increased burden of diarrheal diseases. The drought impact produced 10,169 food insecurity cases. Moreover, there is poor water and sanitation coverage, and the community has low knowledge of dietary diversity. There is a high turnover of government health workers and low technical capacity in CMAM management and essential health service delivery at last-mile health facilities. In this context, GOAL Ethiopia designed a 9-month project (15-Aug-2024–14-May-2025) to address urgent gaps in the malnutrition response in the targeted woreda to reduce the burden of malnutrition and respond to the unmet needs of communities affected by environmental hazards through the implementation of an integrated and multi-sectoral approach and maximize the results while providing a Nutrition, Health, WASH, and Agriculture package of interventions with strong protection to improve the nutrition status of the target population (priority 1). The intervention will be delivered at the community and health facility levels to address factors that have a direct impact onltbrgtmalnutrition, including the availability of water, sanitation, hygiene, agriculture inputs, preventive and curative nutrition services, and access to essential health care services with strong protection and GBV mainstreaming. The project is linked to the 2024 reserve allocation strategy. The selection of the prioritized sectors has been done in consultation with the relevant clusters at the national and regional level and based on the MIRA Assessment findings, taking into consideration also the local stakeholders, who have been consulted during proposal development and have endorsed the proposed activities. This project also considers meaningful inclusion for cross-cutting issues (like AAP, gender, and disability inclusion) and protection mainstreaming-related activities, which are reflected in the log frame. 1.7 Planned Start Date: 15-Aug-2024 Planned End Datelt/pgt
